summary: Iteration 4 backend tested. All 25 new tests for project-wise team masters passed, plus 64 prior regression tests still pass (89/89 = 100%). Verified: Project model has site_engineers[]/project_managers[] arrays; seed idempotently assigns seeded site@ + pm@ to all 3 seeded projects via $addToSet (no duplicates on repeat calls); GET /api/projects correctly filters by role (SE and PM see only assigned; purchase/billing/admin see all); GET /api/projects?all=1 as admin bypasses filter; POST /api/projects/{id}/team is admin-only (403 for all other roles, 404 for missing project, 400 for empty body, returns updated project doc); POST /api/mrf enforces team membership for site_engineer (403 for unassigned, 200 for assigned, 200 after admin assigns); POST /api/mrf/{id}/approve enforces PM team membership (403 for unassigned PM, 200 for assigned PM); GET /api/mrf as PM returns only MRFs from projects where they are a PM; regression on PO create, billing update, admin passthrough, dashboard all pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1722 lines — should be split into modules (auth/, mrf/, po/, billing/, invoice/, projects/) for maintainability (>700 line guideline).
POST /api/projects/{id}/team accepts a raw dict — consider a Pydantic model (TeamUpdate) for consistent validation/OpenAPI docs.
list_projects uses in-Python filtering after fetching all projects; for large project counts consider Mongo-side {'site_engineers': u.user_id} / {'project_managers': u.user_id} query for efficiency.
approve_mrf still allows admin to approve any project MRF (only PM is restricted); this matches spec but worth noting for audit purposes.
MRF create path re-fetches project on every call — acceptable but could be a single find with projection.
seed_data_creation: Uses POST /api/seed (idempotent). Additionally creates ephemeral fresh users with TEST_new_site_<hex>@vasu.dev and TEST_new_pm_<hex>@vasu.dev via dev-login for negative-path tests; these do not collide with seeded data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_project_team.py exercises full team-based access control. If MRF listing count assertions fail in future runs due to test-created MRFs from earlier iterations, prefer assertion-by-project-id-membership (as done here) over count-equals-empty. Fresh users are created per-test-module run; because they are added to VIS-101 by TestProjectTeamUpdate, later tests must accommodate that.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. During test development one assertion incorrectly expected fresh PM to see 0 MRFs after they were already assigned to VIS-101 in a prior test; fixed the assertion to verify only-assigned-projects semantics (which is the actual invariant).
